source_review.notes: Checked current Linux socket, socket creation, accept, recvmsg, networking API, sk_buff, network scaling, BPF socket lookup, cgroup socket-option and SNMP counter documentation. All ten cited URLs returned HTTP 200 after normal redirects; user API contracts, kernel object architecture, illustrative lifecycle models, operational guidance and assurance remain separately scoped.

evidence: Checked descriptor, open file description, generic socket, protocol endpoint, namespace, security context, queue, error, lifecycle, reference and buffer notation.
Reviewed object reachability, final-reclamation predicate, accept-queue bound, memory-accounting bound and time-indexed readiness predicate.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation distinguishes process-local handles, shared file state, generic dispatch, protocol state, namespace ownership, resource accounting and lifecycle generation.

evidence: Executed a completed-connection queue with capacity two and three candidate children.
Confirmed children A and B are accepted exactly once, child C is governed as full, and a second worker observes EAGAIN after stale readiness.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The deterministic queue calculation validates one bounded abstract sequence only; it implements no TCP handshake, locking, memory ordering, timer, descriptor, packet, network namespace or kernel behavior.

evidence: Re-derived the fd-to-file-to-socket-to-protocol reachability chain while retaining independent timer, hash, buffer and callback references.
Checked final reclamation, bounded accept ownership, send and receive charging and readiness revalidation obligations.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The relations are an ownership model and deliberately do not claim a complete formalization of Linux, BSD sockets, TCP, UDP or Unix-domain sockets.

evidence: Reviewed unsupported family tuples, malformed addresses, zero and overflowing iovecs, misaligned ancillary data, ephemeral exhaustion, bind conflict, backlog overflow and accept races.

Reviewed buffer pressure, stale readiness, timeout and cancellation, error queues, zero-copy ownership, duplicate descriptors, namespace transfer, timer-after-close, device loss and hostile packet rates.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Creation, parsing, lookup, passive open, messaging, readiness, memory, asynchronous ownership, teardown, namespace, security and evidence boundaries receive distinct treatment.

evidence: Traced create, descriptor publication, bind, listen, request establishment, accept, connect, send, receive, wait, shutdown, close and final free through twelve obligations.
Verified layered identity, bounded user parsing, namespace-scoped lookup, separate listener queues, race-safe readiness, protocol message semantics, memory charging and callback-safe teardown.
invariant_checking.notes: The chapter treats descriptor state, protocol state, queued data, waiters, credentials, namespaces, callbacks and final reclamation as coupled but independently checkable invariants.

evidence: Reviewed family dispatch, VFS integration, socket and sock objects, bind, listen, accept, connect, message I/O, ancillary data, buffers, readiness, errors, shutdown, references, namespaces and scaling.

Constructed counterexamples for descriptor-as-socket, backlog-as-one-queue, readiness-as-reservation, stream-send-as-record, timeout-as-revocation, close-as-destruction and current-task-as-socket-namespace.
proof_review.notes: The chapter supplies reusable socket-layer obligations, not a formal proof of the Linux kernel, a protocol implementation, network device, BPF policy, application or security boundary.

evidence: Audited uses of created, bound, connected, listening, accepted, readable, writable, queued, sent, delivered, acknowledged, shut down, closed, orphaned and freed.
Confirmed system-call contracts, kernel mechanisms, abstract models, recommendations, empirical examples and assurance claims remain separately scoped.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Writable connect readiness is not labeled success, send acceptance is not labeled peer delivery, close is not labeled final free and zero-copy notification is not labeled remote acknowledgement.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/OS-071/report.json records source, expected and actual output, stderr, exit status, toolchain and environment for the accept-queue model.
Reviewed required family, protocol, namespace, socket identity, options, queue, memory, error, trace, packet, CPU, device, workload and fault evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The passing toy establishes capacity and one stale-readiness outcome only; it provides no evidence for Linux sockets, TCP, accept, memory ordering, concurrency, network traffic, security or performance.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed generic API dispatch, file and protocol object separation, connection lifecycle, messaging, readiness, memory, errors, namespaces, security, teardown, scaling and evidence as one socket architecture.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed current Linux socket interfaces and internals as implementable concerns, including atomic descriptor flags, nonblocking drains, ancillary validation, ownership notification, resource limits, stable diagnostics and teardown races. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from API and object graph through endpoint lifecycle, messaging and readiness, then namespace, policy, scaling and tests, followed by twelve obligations, fifteen trade-offs, twenty-five misconceptions, ten examples and five complete exercises.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external operating-systems academic, Linux networking, transport-protocol, application, security, performance, independent-verification or certification review is claimed.
